definitions.explanation: A two-wheeled passenger cart pulled by a person on foot. Originally a common mode of transportation in the Meiji era, now found as a tourist attraction in places like Asakusa, Kyoto, and Kamakura.

examples.japanese: ⟦{浅草|あさくさ}→浅草：28393_asakusa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{人力車|じんりきしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}った→乗る：00511_noru⟧。
examples.english: I rode a rickshaw in Asakusa.

examples.japanese: {人力車|じんりきしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{車夫|しゃふ}→車夫：18460_shafu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{観光|かんこう}→観光：00173_kankou⟧⟦ガイド→ガイド：05116_gaido⟧もして⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: The rickshaw puller also serves as a sightseeing guide.

examples.japanese: {人力車|じんりきしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{明治時代|めいじじだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{発明|はつめい}→発明：01495_hatsumei⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "human-powered vehicle" (⟦{人力|じんりき}→人力：11714_jinriki⟧ + ⟦{車|しゃ}→車：09874_sha⟧). The English word "rickshaw" is derived from the Japanese {人力車|じんりきしゃ}.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Today, {人力車|じんりきしゃ} are primarily a tourist experience in historic districts. The pullers (⟦{車夫|しゃふ}→車夫：18460_shafu⟧) typically provide narrated tours of the area.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人力車|じんりきしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to ride a rickshaw
- {人力車|じんりきしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}く→引く：01978_hiku⟧: to pull a rickshaw
- ⟦{観光|かんこう}→観光：00173_kankou⟧{人力車|じんりきしゃ}: sightseeing rickshaw
